clue.text: Attic in which Anita foolishly keeps bird

indicators.note: one set of letters keeps, or holds, the bird inside itself
the name Anita is treated foolishly, its letters jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, typically a chicken

explanation.surface: A woman named Anita has carelessly let a bird nest in her loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like a loft but is the definition: Attica was the region around Athens. 'Foolishly' jumbles the name to ATIAN, which 'keeps' the bird inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic is an adjective meaning of Attica or its capital, Athens, so it is a synonym for a citizen of that city.

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to put away food is to eat it, so the past tense is ate

explanation.surface: A man stashed away his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests storing; here it means consumed, as in putting away a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune in the sense of destiny or lot is a synonym for what is fated to happen.

definitions.meaning: a player on good form is said to be ..., read as two words
to keep someone posted is to tell them the latest news

explanation.surface: A coach's two-part instruction to a player.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top form is being 'in form', and keeping someone up to date is the verb meaning to tell or notify.

indicators.note: the word for work sits in the middle of the word for plain language

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A request to write a job invitation in simple words.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite something, such as a toast or a suggestion, is to put it forward, a synonym of proposing it.

parts.note: to groom a horse or person is to dress them, make them neat
a season is a period of time, as is an age

explanation.surface: A stable hand at a three-day horse event over the course of a season.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue. 'Groom' looks like the stable hand; it is the verb meaning to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian contest of three phases, of which the trained-movement arena test is the first, so the answer is one part found in it.

definitions.meaning: a runner who has started the race is said to be away from the starting line
someone mistaken is wide of the target, inaccurate

explanation.surface: Continuing the horse event: a rider who has set off on the wrong idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having got going from the starting line and, figuratively, being wrong or inaccurate.

indicators.note: sloppy suggests the letters of read of are carelessly thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a scruffy piece of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, a specific type of hat.

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of isn't rare are rearranged unexpectedly

explanation.surface: A remark that some kitchen gadget is actually quite common.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sieve or colander used for draining food, an example of a kitchen utensil.

indicators.note: the word for common goes around the letter taken from the town name

parts.note: rife means widespread or common
the head, or first letter, of Leather is L; Leatherhead is also a town in Surrey

explanation.surface: A report that looting is widespread in the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a commuter town in Surrey, England; read as Leather's head it gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle somewhere is to search through it and steal from it, a synonym of plunder.

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An ambassador is about to receive a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Present in the sense of in attendance or at this place is a synonym.

definitions.meaning: read playfully as OP, short for opus, a work, followed by a word for place

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is hostility among colleagues at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning split of workplace into work and place: OP plus POSITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is hostility, a synonym of resistance from the other side.

parts.note: Vic is a boy's name, short for Victor
Tim is a boy's name, short for Timothy

explanation.surface: An instruction to fool a pair of lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is someone tricked or taken in, the same as a target of a scam.

clue.text: One ending a period in a degenerate uprising

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as in a school term

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising turns the word for degenerate upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: to rot is to decay or degenerate

explanation.surface: Someone who brought an era to a close during a failed revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks like a revolt; in a down clue it means reading upwards, so ROT becomes TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ends or finishes things off; the word is formed from the verb meaning to end.

clue.text: Plan case differently? That's held in the balance

indicators.note: differently signals that the letters of plan case are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether to set out a legal case another way, with the outcome uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in the balance' suggests uncertainty; it literally means part of a weighing balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of weighing scales has dishes on which goods are weighed, each part of the balance.

parts.note: rude means offensive or impolite

explanation.surface: Someone interferes and in time becomes insulting.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere where unwanted, a synonym of barging in.

clue.text: Managed without fur that's rendered unserviceable

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for managed goes outside the fur

parts.note: did means managed, as in 'did well enough'
sable is a valuable fur from a small mammal

explanation.surface: Coping without a fur coat that has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking; here it is the old sense 'outside', so the word for managed wraps around the fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put out of action or made unusable has been incapacitated.

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'You're joking!'

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to run, firmly refusing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a verb meaning to escape and an exclamation of incredulity.

clue.text: Operatic heroine hides in a barrel? Strange!

indicators.note: the heroine hides inside the abbreviation for barrel

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for barrel
Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: A singer from an opera concealed inside a cask: how odd!
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary or unusual is strange.

clue.text: Student has little support when bad weather intervenes

indicators.note: the bad weather comes between, splitting the word for little support

parts.note: a tee is a small peg supporting a golf ball
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A student gets little help when a storm interrupts.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, the tee is the little peg that holds up the ball, hence 'little support'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learning a trade or being taught is a learner, a student.

clue.text: Emperor backed morning scripture lessons in India …

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, morning
RI is religious instruction, school scripture lessons
a tsar was the emperor of Russia; backed says he stands behind, so comes last

explanation.surface: A ruler supported early-morning Bible classes during the Raj.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, which is also in India.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in the Punjab, home of the Sikh Golden Temple, so a place found in that country.

clue.text: Intelligence services see note that's taken from a dupe

parts.note: MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6
the letter C is named 'see'
a key is a note on a piano or a musical key

explanation.surface: Spies see a message that has been lifted from someone they fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the mickey is to mock someone, so the mickey is what is taken from a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'take the mickey' means to tease or ridicule, and a dupe is the butt of such teasing.

indicators.note: the relatives are placed inside the abbreviation for India

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Continuing the Indian theme: also family members living in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Repaying in the same way or manner is an idiom equivalent to doing it likewise.

indicators.note: disturbed signals that the letters of singer are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist interrupted an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical artist, an example of a painter.

clue.text: Get out jewellery for outdoor pursuit

parts.note: scram is a slang command to go away
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Swap your jewellery for an activity in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing over rough rocky ground using hands and feet is a hillwalking activity, an example of an outdoor pursuit.

explanation.surface: Plunder taken in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils of war' reads as loot; split, it is a verb plus a description of the Roman war god.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means damages, and is also the name of the Roman deity of war.

clue.text: Came across Zionist leader in France

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

indicators.note: leader indicates the first letter of Zionist

explanation.surface: Meeting a Zionist leader somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in Lorraine, north-eastern France, so a place found in that country.

clue.text: European turns to Spain for escape

indicators.note: the word for European turns round, reading backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A European heads for Spain to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks like the letter E; it is POLE, while Spain gives the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off, especially secretly to marry, is a kind of escape.

clue.text: Impartial trade union meets a Labour leader after a time

parts.note: even-handed or even means fair and impartial

indicators.note: leader indicates the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A fair-minded union meets a Labour politician after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens finally or in the end, after some time has passed, is ultimate.
